purpose: Calibration anchors for the lane-63 label-world generator (src/gems63/worlds.py). These are ASSUMPTIONS with stated provenance, not measured scores.

shift_prior.metric: componentwise cap |dy|,|dx| <= 4 px (Chebyshev); directions uniform over the 8 lattice directions
anchors: Prompt-cited Hermant et al. measurement: catalogue offsets up to 400 m (= 4 px at the 100 m grid). The paper itself is not fetchable from this sandbox's allowlist (IR-63-09); the figure is carried with that provenance.
Organizer statement (competition problem page, prompt-cited): Phase-2 faults may be added, removed or changed — motivates the omission + decoy components.

Family drift evidence: 60GEMSDOE evidence/h33_holdout.json shows a large gap between raw and drift-corrected holdout means on the gems32 instrument (e.g. D2.8-Poisson300m-Ref 0.0983 raw vs 0.1480 drift-corrected), demonstrating that geometric perturbation of the truth materially changes scores.

decoys.policy: one decoy segment per dropped component, same pixel size, uniform placement inside the scored (active) domain, orientation uniform over [0,180)
decoys.anchor: prompt instruction 'add decoy segments at the observed density' — expected segment count per world is held equal to the withheld count

honesty_note: The world generator is only as honest as these anchors. If the true Phase-2 motion distribution differs, the CVaR ranking can change. No public-leaderboard tuning was used anywhere in the pipeline.
